[b]Balatro[/b] is a roguelite deckbuilder pretending to be a pixel-art poker game.  I know everyone's at least heard of it at this point, [i]but[/i] I've 100%'d it 2.5 times on mobile and wrote this to figure out where my life went wrong.  

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[b]Balatro[/b] eases you into madness: You start with a basic deck of 54 cards, score points on traditional poker hands, and earn money.   Spend that money on upgrades: joker cards that alter scoring, "tarot cards" that upgrade your deck, and "celestial" cards that increase point yields.  It seems so simple.  

And then it goes off the rails.

You're constantly unlocking new decks that behave in unique ways, new jokers that add crazy nuance and multipliers, new ways to score, etc.  "Spectral" cards tempt you to risk everything in exchange for massive gains.  New difficulties force you to level up faster.  Before you know it, you've spent an entire overnight flight trying to score a hand with five gold sevens of clubs, and have yet to sleep a wink.

[h3]What Works For Me[/h3]
✅ I actually love the artwork.  It's so dumb and so simple, but some of the jokers are just… the best.

✅ I did not understand poker or poker hands before [b]Balatro[/b], but "Run Info" includes a simple visual guide that makes more sense than any video I've ever watched.

✅ The card synergies!  The absolute insanity you can create with some Magicians and a Lucky Cat, or a King, a Mime, and a lot of chariots, red seals, and demonic deer!  

✅ Players

I've recently started playing Balatro on my phone. She first noticed when she said, "Hey that music's pretty good. What is it?" 
 
So I started showing her the game. She got hooked. In fact, she started asking me if I could play Balatro in bed so she could watch it before she fell asleep. She claims it's relaxing. 
 
From here, she started asking questions. 
 
"Why do you keep picking flush? Pick something else, it's boring." 
 
"OOO that joker's shiny! Can you buy it? No? What do you mean you can't?" 
 
"What's a straight?" 
 
"Can you choose the stardew valley cards?" 
 
"Why did you sell that one? That one's your favorite!" 
 
"You want me to buy it? No I don't want to play. I like watching you!" 
 
"Why did you throw away an ACE!?" 
 
"Can you level up something else please?" 
 
"Why don't you play pairs? Stop throwing away pairs." 
 
"Is this a straight?" 
 
"Choose the tarot pack! Wait, why do you keep checking the description for Death? What do you mean you forget?" 
 
Now, every night, regardless of when we go to bed or how busy we've been all day - she asks me to play Balatro. 
 
If I dare say no, she looks as if I broke her heart. 
 
So, I eventually say yes. And then she lays on my shoulder and watches me lose, having a great time the whole way through. 
 
Is anyone else experiencing something like this? Let me know.
If gambling addiction already runs in your family, then this is just the game for you.

OVERVIEW  
Balatro is a Poker inspired strategic card game for PC that combines elements of deck-building, turn-based tactics, and roguelike progression. Players must assemble and refine their deck of cards to navigate through demanding battles. Each card represents different actions and abilities, and the player must manage resources wisely to outwit the score requirements and boss skills


UNIQUE TRAITS:
Unlike many card games where the deck-building and progression are linear, Balatro features a dynamic deck evolution system. As you play, the cards you acquire can change and evolve based on your choices, making the deck-building experience feel fresh every time.

GAMEPLAY:
At its core, Balatro follows the familiar structure of turn-based combat found in many card games. Players start with a basic deck of cards and build it up over time by acquiring new cards or upgrading existing ones. Each turn, you draw a hand of cards. Resource management is key, as you need to carefully plan your moves to avoid depleting your resources too quickly.

GRAPHICS:
Balatro features card designs beautifully crafted, with each card illustration being rich in detail and moody in tone. 
The visual effects during battles are satisfying without being overly flashy, allowing the strategic elements to remain the focus. 

BOSSES:
Battles feel like puzzles that require a mix of preparation and adaptability. You’ll need to constantly adjust your strategies to win.

[h2]TLDR:[/h2] A roguelike deckbuilding game that is easy to learn and difficult to master, accompanied a complex difficulty curve that will ultimately test the patience of most players. 
 
[h2]GAMEPLAY OVERVIEW:[/h2] On the surface, Balatro looks like a run-of-the-mill poker-style game with colorful graphics, but the reality is that is so much more than that. 
 
Basic gameplay functions much like draw poker, with the player (normally) drawing eight cards to make standard poker hands (pairs, two pairs, straights, flushes, etc.). Each hand has a chip value (AKA, points) and multiplier, which are used to determine the chip total for that hand. The player proceeds through the antes (rounds), with each each ante made up of a small blind, big blind, and one of thirty boss blinds, each with its own creative name. Most often, the player has four hands to play and three chances to discard/draw in order to beat each blind. The first two blinds only have chip goals to beat, while the boss blind adds a wrinkle, such as negating all the cards of a given suit or reducing hand size by one. On defeating the boss blind, the ante increases, along with the required chip totals to beat the next set of blinds. 
 
Again, it all seems simple enough but the diabolically clever element comes in the form of the jokers. Defeating blinds reward the players with cash, which can be spent between blinds, and the most pressing purchase will usually be jokers, all with colorful names and unique artwork. Som

[h1]Why Is Balatro So Good?[/h1]

Balatro might genuinely be one of the best games ever made. But what exactly makes this game so damn good?

Before I actually try to answer that, there is one thing I want to get out of the way. [b]You do not need to know anything about poker to play Balatro.[/b] In fact, that was probably the first thing that came to my mind when I first saw the game. I thought I would need to understand poker hands, strategies and all the rules that come with it.

You really don't.

[hr]

[h2]So what actually is Balatro?[/h2]

Let me give you a very simplified idea of what Balatro actually is.

You start with a deck of cards and your goal is pretty simple. You play different combinations of cards to reach a certain score. Reach the required score and you beat the round. Then you move on to the next one. You keep doing this until you reach [b]Ante 8[/b], which you can basically think of as the final level.

Sounds simple enough.

But this is where things start getting interesting.

Alongside your normal playing cards, Balatro has around [b]150 unique Joker cards[/b]. Every Joker can completely change how you approach the game. They have different rarities, different abilities and even different variations of the same Joker.

Then you have Tarot cards, Planet cards, Spectral cards and a whole bunch of other things that interact with your deck in different ways.

But honestly, you don't even need to understand all of that right now.
